*Moth's hat of names grows thinner every night: the salt sellers, wool carters and spice peddlers are not getting through. The bristle boars on the Tusk Path drive the traders off the road. Thin them.*

    - Evening. It is evening, is it not? Good. Anything earlier I refuse to discuss. This is the hat. Every name in it is a stall, and every evening I draw them out, first name, first pick, the way the first traders did. Lately I count the names first. That never used to be necessary.
    - No salt seller in a month. The wool carters, twice since spring. The spice peddler who smelled of cloves from three stalls away: gone. Shade brings a few in, but even Shade says the boar have taken the **Tusk Path**, and a cart that meets a boar turns round.
    - Corners stand empty for nights now, and the market feeds half the city through the winter. Clear the road for them: **50 [Bristle Boar](../monsters/bristle_boar.md)s** on [The Tusk Path](../maps/tusk_path.md). I would go myself, but it would mean being awake at a reasonable hour.
    - Through the Outworks, into the Bristlewood, up to the hill path with the tracks too big for comfort. Come back after dark. I will be here. I am always here after dark.
    - Fair. Into the hat goes another empty fold of paper, then. I will draw it out and pretend it is a trader.
    - Fifty bristle boars on the Tusk Path. I counted the hat again tonight. Same number as last night, minus one.
